name: Sikafloor-305 W
paste:
SIKAFLOOR®-305 W: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-305 W, April 2023, Version 03.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikafloor_-305_w.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-305 W where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-305 W is a two part water based, low VOC, polyurethane, coloured matt seal coat.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sikafloor®-305 W may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Matt seal coat for Sika ComfortFloor® flooring range, for smooth Sikafloor® Multiflex polyurethanes and for the Sikafloor® Multidur epoxy range.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.11.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-305 W
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-part PUR matt coloured seal coat for use with Sika Comfortfloor®, MultDur® and MultiFlex® flooring ranges
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability. VOC Emission certificate according to AgBB und DIBt approval requirements (AgBB – Committee for Health-related Evaluation of Building Products, DiBt – German Institute for Building Technology), Eurofins report No. 769855D
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - Synthetic resin screed material according to EN 13813:2002, Declaration of Performance and provided with the CE marking.
    - Coating for surface protection of concrete according to EN 1504-2:2004, Declaration of Performance 0208010400500000031041, certified by notified factory production control certification body 0620, and provided with the CE marking.
    - Fire classification acc. to EN 13501-1, Test reports 08-198, 08-199 and CR-13- 167/1, Ghent University
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 13813:2002: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13501-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - ISO 2813: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Gloss level (p.2).
    - DIN 53 505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Abrasion resistance (p.2).
    - EN 13892-8: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Water based
    - Very low odour
    - Good UV and yellowing resistance
    - Easy to clean
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: PUR
    - Appearance and colour: Sikafloor®-305 W is matt after final curing. Available in various colour shades and as substrates for local tinting.
2.7 Density.
    | Part A | ~1,33 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~1,13 kg/l |
    | Mixed resin | ~1,18 kg/l |
    | All Density values at +23 °C |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Tensile adhesion strength: >1,5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika technical service for specific information.
2.9 Gloss level.
    | Angle | Value |
    | 85° | < 50 |
    | 60° | < 10 |
    Test method printed: (ISO 2813)
2.10 Shore D Hardness.
    | ~84 | (7 days / +23 °C) |
    Test method printed: (DIN 53 505)
2.11 Abrasion resistance.
    | <1000 mg | (H22/1000/1000) |
    Test method printed: (ISO 868)
2.12 Systems. Please refer to the System Data Sheet of:
    | Sika Comfortfloor® PS-23 | Seamless, smooth, unicolour, low |
    | voc, elastic polyurethane floor covering |
    | Sika Comfortfloor® PS-27 | Seamless, smooth, unicolour, low |
    | voc, tough elastic polyurethane floor covering |
    | Sika Comfortfloor® PS-63 | Seamless, smooth, unicolour, low |
    | voc, sound insulating elastic polyurethane floor covering |
    | Sika Comfortfloor® PS-65 | Seamless, smooth, unicolour, low |
    | voc, resilient polyurethane floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PS-32 UV | Smooth, unicolour, tough elastic |
    | polyurethane floor covering with sealer |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.13 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C.
2.14 Packaging.
    | Part A | 8,5 kg containers |
    | Part B | 1,5 kg containers |
    | Part A+B | 10 kg ready to mix units |
2.15 Shelf life.
    | Part A | 6 months from date of production |
    | Part B | 12 months from date of production |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 85 : 15 (by weight)
4.3 Consumption. ~0,13–0,15 kg/m²/layer; This figure is theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level and wastage etc. When used in high wear conditions, for example where rolling office chairs occur, a double layer Sikafloor®-305 W is highly advisable. A double layer is increasing the mechanical strength of the system and it resistance against office chairs particularly.
4.4 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~80 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~60 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~30 minutes |
    | Caution: End of potlife is not noticeable. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Curing time. Before overcoating Sikafloor®-305 W allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10 °C | 24 hours | 4 days |
    | +20 °C | 16 hours | 3 days |
    | +30 °C | 12 hours | 2 days |
    Based on relative humidity of max. 70 % and good ventilation. Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
4.6 Applied product ready for use.
    | Temperature | Foot traffic | Light traffic | Full cure |
    | +10 °C | ~30 hours | ~48 hours | ~6 days |
    | +20 °C | ~16 hours | ~24 hours | ~4 days |
    | +30 °C | ~12 hours | ~18 hours | ~3 days |
    Note: Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions
4.7 Mixing. Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 3 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. During the mixing of the Components A and B add 5–7 % of clean water. To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. After mixing give the material a rest for 10 minutes. Over mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment.
4.8 Mixing - Mixing Tools. Sikafloor®-305 W must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300–400 rpm) or other suitable equipment.
4.9 Application. Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative humidity and dew point. Uniformly spread Sikafloor®-305 W by using a short pile nylon roller. Sikafloor®-305 W can also be applied by using airless spray equipment. A seamless finish can be achieved if a “wet” edge is maintained during application.
4.10 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.11 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-305 W must be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 7 days (+20 °C).
    - Unevenness of substrates as well as inclusions of dirt cannot be covered by thin sealers coats. Therefore substrate and adjacent areas must be cleaned thoroughly prior to application.
    - When applying on an epoxy surface, the floor has to be sanded with preferably, a green 3M pad to secure a proper adhesion.
    - If heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
4.12 Further information - Substrate Quality & Preparation. Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
4.13 Further information - Application Instructions.
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Maintenance
    - Please refer to “Sikafloor®- CLEANING REGIME”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 75 % max. During curing the relative humidity should not exceed 75 %. Adequate fresh air ventilation must be provided to remove the excess moisture from the curing product.
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.11):
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-305 W must be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 7 days (+20 °C).
5.7 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | ~1,33 kg/l; Part B | ~1,13 kg/l; Mixed resin | ~1,18 kg/l; All Density values at +23 °C (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Gloss level: Angle | Value; 85° | < 50; 60° | < 10 (ISO 2813)
    - Shore D Hardness: ~84 | (7 days / +23 °C) (DIN 53 505)
    - Abrasion resistance: <1000 mg | (H22/1000/1000) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: >1,5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-305 W, April 2023, Version 03.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikafloor_-305_w.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SikaFloor 305 W Part A, version 29/08/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/MSDS%20Sikafloor-305%20W%20Part%20A%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-305 W Part A, version 21/01/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/b/sds-sikafloor-305wparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Directive 2004/42/ce limitation of emissions of.
    - VOC
    - According to the EU-Directive 2004/42, the maximum allowed content of VOC (Product category IIA / j type wb) is 140 g/l (Limit 2010) for the ready to use product.
    - The maximum content of Sikafloor®-305 W is < 140 g/l VOC for the ready to use product.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
